source.title: Open problems on nonlinear dominated operators in locally bounded spaces of measurable functions

needs_review.question_text_raw: A visually inspected candidate on article page 57 appears to concern existence of a majorant or exact majorant for a nonlinear dominated operator, but complete verbatim source text could not be recovered from the PDF.

A visually inspected candidate on article page 58 appears to concern conditions under which a nonlinear operator has a regular majorant, but complete verbatim source text could not be recovered from the PDF.

A visually inspected candidate on article pages 59-60 appears to concern applying dominated nonlinear operators and their majorants to systems of Hammerstein nonlinear integral equations, but complete verbatim source text could not be recovered from the PDF.

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH record 1050.47056 / 2097467 to exact work by V. G. Fetisov, Vladikavkaz. Mat. Zh. 5:1 (2003), pages 57-61. zbMATH was used only as a resolver; exact-work full-text links were found at EuDML, EMIS, VMJ, and MathNet.Ru.
Downloaded the exact-work PDF from http://www.vmj.ru/articles/2003_1_9.pdf to the local temporary path recorded in source.resolved_locator.

Mapped the full-text PDF as a five-page Russian article, article pages 57-61. The PDF contains the article title, introductory definitions of nonlinear dominated operators and majorants, discussion of regular majorants and nonlinear integral operators, applications to Hammerstein systems, and references. Embedded text extraction with pypdf produced unusable encoded text, so visual extraction was attempted.

Visual inspection suggested a candidate open problem on article page 57 about existence of a majorant or exact majorant for nonlinear dominated operators, but no complete verbatim statement could be recovered.
Visual inspection suggested a candidate open problem on article page 58 about regular majorants for nonlinear operators, but no complete verbatim statement could be recovered.

Visual inspection suggested a candidate open direction on article pages 59-60 about Hammerstein systems and dominated nonlinear integral operators, but no complete verbatim statement could be recovered.
